references.text: The Holy Place (הַקֹּדֶשׁ) refers to the innermost room of the tabernacle, behind the veil, where the ark of the covenant stood.
A young bull (פַר בֶּן־בָּקָר) is used as a sin offering, as prescribed at the consecration of the priests.
The sin offering (חַטָּאת) with a young bull was required for the high priest when he sinned.
The ram (אַיִל) as a burnt offering (עֹלָה) was a common sacrifice that was completely burned on the altar.
Aaron's sin-offering bull is mentioned again later in the chapter as atonement for himself and his household.
Annual atonement on the incense altar with the blood of the sin offering, connected to the Day of Atonement.
The offerings on the Day of Atonement, including a bull as a sin offering and a ram as a burnt offering.
The high priest entered the Most Holy Place once a year, not without blood, which he offered for himself and the sins of the people.
Christ entered the holy place once for all, not with the blood of goats and calves, but with his own blood.
Christ entered heaven itself to appear before God's presence on our behalf, unlike the high priest who entered the holy place every year.
